claims.text: The initial Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy contains both amorphous and crystalline phases.
Cooling at 100 K/s followed by reheating at 10 K/min will increase amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Cooling at 100 K/s followed by reheating at 10 K/min will increase the thermal stability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The proposed cooling and reheating protocol suppresses extensive primary crystallization.
The structural mediator is suppression of primary non-eutectic phases.
Control of cooling and reheating rates kinetically controls crystallization.
Cooling and reheating rates influence crystalline-phase nucleation.
Cooling and reheating rates influence crystalline-phase growth.
The proposed protocol will produce a 20% increase in amorphous retention relative to the reported behavior.
The proposed protocol will produce a 50 K increase in thermal stability relative to the reported behavior.
The relevant operating boundary spans cooling rates from 10 to 1000 K/s.
The relevant operating boundary spans reheating rates from 1 to 100 K/min.
The exact optimized cooling and reheating protocol may depend on experimental conditions and equipment.

contradictions.description: The predicted gains are 20% amorphous retention and 50 K thermal stability, but the falsification rule uses lower thresholds of 10% and 20 K. Results between these values would fail to achieve the stated prediction without falsifying it, making the test non-decisive for the quantitative hypothesis.
